dataset: dHCP fetal atlas GW21-GW36 (parcellations_scaled), cropped from the area-band sampler output
paths_note: band_root is machine-specific and deliberately empty here. Copy this file to configs/crop_band_config_dhcp_atlas.json (gitignored) and point it at the sampler's atlas output root (the folder holding GW21..GW36), or at a single GW folder to crop one week.
bbox_note: Atlas-specific: these are fractions of the rendered frame, which is 221x180 axial (axis_z), 180x180 coronal (axis_y), 180x221 sagittal (axis_x). Do NOT reuse the fetal_surface numbers - that dataset has different frame sizes AND a different orientation. Sagittal is left null because it is not cropped, as in the previous dataset.
orientation_note: The sampler renders each slice as flipud of the volume slice (verified: IoU 1.000 against the label volume). Volume axes are (L, A, S), so image rows run left->right hemisphere top-to-bottom, and image columns run posterior->anterior on axis_z and inferior->superior on axis_y. The interhemispheric midline sits at y = 0.494 on every week, axis and slice.
roi_note: Each ROI is the left hemisphere's outer corner: bottom edge exactly on the midline (y = 0.4944 -> row 89 of 180, so the opposite hemisphere is excluded), holding the lateral ventricle at the inner edge together with the outer brain boundary and background beyond it. axis_z takes the anterior/frontal pole, axis_y the superior/vertex end. Both crops are 56x70 px = 28x35 mm, portrait (w/h 0.80). The coronal box was recovered by template-matching the reference crop supplied by the user (matched GW25 axis_y s04 at px 109,19-165,90, IoU 0.90); the axial box mirrors its size and framing. Deep gray is deliberately NOT the target: the crop is narrowed past basal ganglia and thalamus. They still enter at the inner edge on some slices, because the lateral ventricle sits directly against them - excluding them on every slice is only possible by moving the box off the tissue entirely, which drops the tissue fill to 26-34% and, on the axial, loses the ventricle on 192 of 320 slices.
fallback_note: fallback_to_auto is false on purpose. With it true, any slice whose manual bbox holds less than min_foreground_pixels is silently replaced by an auto-detected bbox, so one folder would mix two different ROIs. False makes such a slice skip loudly instead.
scale_bar_note: pixel_size_mm is the parent slice's voxel spacing - cropping is pure pixel slicing with no resample, so the crop keeps it. The bar is then a real distance, round(mm / pixel_size_mm) columns wide. scale_bar_mm is left null so the auto-picker takes the longest round length fitting scale_bar_max_width_frac: 10 mm = 20 px at this 56 px crop width. Do NOT pin it to 20 mm to match the full slices - 20 mm is 40 px here, 71 percent of the frame. Never calibrate pixel size from a drawn bar.
scale_bar_position_note: Side of the crop the bar strip goes on. "bottom" matches where the sampler puts it on the full slices, so neither output has the bar lying on the section. "top" is the older placement and remains the default, so the fetal_surface config is unaffected.
scale_bar_gap_note: Clearance between the section and the bar for bottom placement, as a fraction of the crop height: 0.12 of a 70 px band is 8 rows. The earlier behaviour scaled the gap off the padding instead and left only 2 rows, close enough that the bar read as part of the image. It is what makes the output 56x93 rather than 56x89; the cropped region itself is unchanged at 56x70.
legacy_note: Only used when pixel_size_mm is null, in which case the bar is a fraction of the crop width and its label is not a measurement.
